title: Instruction Fermentation - Few-shot Mixes & Failure Probes
content:
Quick notes + scratch experiments for the few-shot mix approach I've been noodling on. This is a messy running log — rough priorities, ad-hoc examples, and failure probes to try next.

Top-level idea
- "Fermentation" metaphor: let a diverse small set of exemplars (style + factual + counterexample) ‘bake’ together in-context so the model infers an instruction transformation strategy rather than pure pattern match.
- Hypothesis: mixing exemplars that vary along orthogonal axes (tone, explicitness, constraint strictness) reduces brittle instruction-following when the user query diverges slightly from training distribution.

Motivation / observed failure modes we're trying to address
- Instruction drift across turns: model starts complying with an earlier, narrower constraint instead of the fresh explicit ask.
- Overly literal templates: hallucination when few-shot examples are too prescriptive.
- Failure to prioritize constraints (e.g., "must cite source" vs "be concise").
- Token budget waste when many long exemplars are included.

Design constraints
- Keep total exemplar tokens <= 1200 for hosted low-latency route (target rwd-xl-13b family with q4).
- Prefer 3–5 exemplars per shotset, leaning to 4 when mixing orthogonally.
- Use short explicit meta-instruction line above exemplars: single sentence (<= 30 tokens) to bias the interpretative frame.

Example meta-instruction (drafts)
- "Answer concisely and label sources when present; follow the style in examples."
- "Prioritize factual accuracy; if unsure, say 'unknown' and propose two plausible next steps."
- "Return JSON with keys 'answer' and 'confidence' unless asked otherwise."

Candidate few-shot mix (4 exemplars, intentionally varied)
--- EX1 (concise factual, explicit source) ---
Q: "What's the capital of Burkina Faso?"
A: "Ouagadougou. Source: CIA World Factbook (2024)."
--- EX2 (friendly, exploratory, hedged) ---
Q: "Where do people go to surf in Portugal?"
A: "Try Nazaré for big waves, Ericeira for consistent surf culture — depends on experience level. Suggest checking local break reports."
--- EX3 (instruction with transformation + constraint) ---
Q: "Summarize the paper 'Sparse Attention with Overlaps' in two sentences and include one critical weakness."
A: "[two-sentence summary]. Weakness: limited evaluation on long-form dialogue where overlapping contexts matter."
--- EX4 (counterexample — hallucination guard) ---
Q: "Who invented the Frindle handwriting protocol?"
A: "Unknown — no credible source found. Possible confusion with a fictional term. Recommend search in DB or decline."

Rationale for ordering: concise factual -> hedged contextual -> transformation constraint -> counterexample. Intuition: lead with high-certainty patterns, then show hedging, then show task-specific transformation and an explicit refusal pattern.

Failure probes to run (quick tests)
- Probe A: Reorder exemplars (counterexample earlier) and measure hallucination rate across 100 dev prompts.
- Probe B: Replace meta-instruction with an implicit one (remove explicit source/citation mention) and measure citation recall.
- Probe C: Increase exemplar token-length individually to see latency vs quality inflection point.
- Probe D: Insert a noisy long example (irrelevant but syntactically similar) to test robustness to distractors.

Evaluation signals to record
- Hallucination rate (binary per-response).
- Instr-consistency score (does response obey latest explicit constraint?) — annotator label for now.
- Token cost per response + median latency (95th percentile).
- Editing distance between candidate completion and exemplar patterns (cheap proxy for overfitting).

Small AB test plan (manual, short-run)
1) Baseline: canonical few-shot set we use today (2–3 identical-format exemplars).
2) Fermentation mix: the 4-exemplar mix above.
3) Hybrid: same mix but with meta-instruction removed.
Run N=200 prompts sampled from: support tickets (anonymized), search queries, and product FAQ edits. Annotate for hallucination + constraint adherence.

Notes / loose TODOs
- [ ] Add automated script to generate mixed exemplars from our curated exemplar bank (repo: prompt-library). See PR #842 for starter generator; can extend to enforce token budget.
- [ ] Tag exemplars with axes: tone=(concise|hedged|formal), constraint=(cite|transform|decline), domain=(fact|opinion|instr). Build small schema in exemplar metadata.
- [ ] Add a synthetic adversarial set where user instructions deliberately contradict earlier examples to observe fallback behavior.
- [ ] Try the mix on private deployment (VPC) to check if latency SLO holds with 1k token context.

Open questions / micro-hypotheses
- Q: Does counterexample placement matter more than exemplar count? (Hypothesis: placement matters more — early counterexample primes refusal patterns.)
- Q: Can short explicit meta-instructions outweigh exemplar ordering? (Hypothesis: meta-instruction is strong when <= 30 tokens, but loses effect if exemplars show contradictory behavior.)
- Q: Are hedged exemplars improving safety or just increasing evasive responses? (annotator needed)

Quick sketch of minimal annotator rubric (for pilot)
- Hallucination: 0/1 (1 if fabricated facts with no reference in known corpora).
- Adherence: 0/1/2 (2=fully obeys latest explicit constraint; 1=partially; 0=ignores).
- Style match: 0/1 (1 if style requested in meta-instr respected).

Slack threads to update
- #prompt-labs: post initial AB plan and ask for 3 volunteer annotators.
- #model-onboarding: sanity-check exemplar labeling schema.

Notes to self (stream-of-consciousness)
- Keep the 'refusal/counterexample' short and formulaic so model can emulate easily.
- Avoid multi-sentence counterexamples that model might mimic as 'how to refuse badly'.
- Consider a small 'sanity exemplar' that always shows "I don't know" so the model learns an explicit refusal token pattern.

Quick command example for running locally (pseudo)
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-xl-13b-q4", "context": "[meta]\n[ex1]\n[ex2]\n[ex3]\n[ex4]\nUser: ...", "max_tokens": 256 }'

Logbook entries to add after experiment runs
- number of examples tried, tokens per exemplar, seed (if deterministic), model name, latency p95, hallucination rate, adherence rate, short notes on surprising failure cases.

End notes
- This is exploratory and intentionally weird; goal is to find high-gain low-cost exemplar patterns that generalize across domains.
- Next edit: flesh out automated generator and annotation UI so we can scale beyond manual N=200 pilots.
